patch.value: A measurement ratchet bound stops enforcing the moment its owner reaches a terminal status, so every guarded population goes unbounded exactly when its fix ships

The tracker measurement ratchet enforces a bound only while the item that owns it is open. The evaluator computes retired as TERMINAL_OWNER_STATUSES.includes(ownerStatus) with TERMINAL_OWNER_STATUSES frozen to closed and canceled, and a retired declaration short-circuits to ok true with reason retired_with_owner before any comparison runs. The header states the rationale directly: bounds retire themselves so that no bound outlives the property it guards, and honest work never needs a waiver to close.

That rationale contains a category error. The property a declaration guards is a population count over the record, such as the number of dependency rows of kind blocks. That population exists for as long as the graph exists. What terminates when the owning item closes is the remediation work, not the property. Retirement is therefore keyed to the lifetime of the fix and applied to the lifetime of the measurement, and the two are not the same interval. A ratchet exists precisely to hold ground after a fix ships; this one releases the ground at that exact moment.

Measured live on 2026-08-09 at commit 9a0a048b6, with the gate reporting twenty-three enforced and three retired declarations. Every one of the twenty-three enforced declarations sits at observed equal to bound exactly. The only declarations whose observed value has drifted away from its declaration are the retired ones. dependency-kind-blocks declares a ceiling of 241 measured on 2026-08-04 and observes 243. dependency-kind-related-to declares a ceiling of 43 and observes 50. Both report ok true with reason retired_with_owner. Both owners, pm-jkbqt8 and pm-4020c5, reached closed at 2026-08-08 around 23:25Z, and the rows that carried each population past its ceiling were written earlier the same evening, between 21:55Z and 22:50Z, by ordinary maintenance sessions using the supported surface. The breach therefore existed while the bounds were still enforced and was never reported, because the next evaluation of the gate ran after the owners had closed and the declarations had retired.

Neither individual retirement is wrong, and this item does not propose reversing either. Both fixes are real and were verified in a sandbox at this commit. Writing a dependency of kind related_to now canonicalizes to related on write, so that population is frozen legacy residue. A reverse blocks row now correctly classifies its dependent as blocked under pm next, so blocks rows are no longer invisible to the readiness resolver. The defect is that the vocabulary offers no way to record the state those two correct decisions should have produced. A declaration is either enforced against a stale number or retired into no enforcement at all. There is no third state meaning the fix shipped, the population is correct at its current value, and it may not grow again. That third state is what a ratchet is for, and it is unexpressible.

Three consequences follow, all observable in the current document.

The guarded population becomes unbounded and unmeasured. The count of blocks rows is 243 today with nothing enforcing it. blocks remains a writable dependency kind, so if the corpus-aware reverse resolution regresses, or a maintenance pass adds ordering rows in the invisible direction again, no declaration counts them.

The declared number freezes and silently misrepresents itself. The re-baseline path in buildUpdatedDeclarations returns the declaration untouched when entry.retired is true, so the update flag can never refresh a retired observation. The document therefore carries 241 with measured_on 2026-08-04 next to declarations that are current, with nothing in the file marking it as neither current nor enforced.

Cancellation silences a guard exactly as closure does. canceled is a member of TERMINAL_OWNER_STATUSES, so abandoning remediation retires the bound on identical terms to completing it. The gate's own failure guidance names this as the remedy, telling a reader that re-declaring is not the remedy and to move the owning item to a terminal status to retire the bound. The cheapest such move is cancellation. A failing ratchet can therefore be silenced by one status mutation, the gate then reports ok true, and nothing in the report distinguishes a guard dropped because the hazard is gone from a guard dropped because the work stopped.

The correct polarity already exists in the same directory and is not shared. The surface replication gate honours a waiver only while it names a pm item and carries an expires_on date that is greater than or equal to today, so a suppression there decays and enforcement resumes automatically. The measurement ratchet inverts this: the bound decays and enforcement ends permanently. Two gates in one directory, opposite lifetime polarities, with nothing reconciling them.

The remedy is a declared disposition for what happens when an owner reaches a terminal status, defaulting to continued enforcement rather than silence, with explicit retirement requiring a recorded reason, and with cancellation never retiring a bound implicitly.

A declaration records what happens when its owner reaches a terminal status, and the default is continued enforcement rather than silence; Explicit retirement requires a recorded reason naming why the guarded property stopped mattering, and a retirement without one fails the gate; A canceled owner never retires a bound implicitly, because abandoning remediation is not evidence that the hazard is gone; A held declaration keeps reporting its observed value and drift, so no number in the document is both stale and indistinguishable from a current one; dependency-kind-blocks and dependency-kind-related-to are re-declared at their true current counts and held, so both populations are guarded against regrowth; A negative control proves that a held bound fails when its population grows after the owner closed

value.text:
Evidence, measured and then shipped in one pass at commit 9a0a048b6.

Measurement before the change. The gate reported twenty-three enforced and three retired declarations. All twenty-three enforced declarations sat at observed equal to bound exactly. The only declarations whose observed value had drifted from what they declared were the retired ones: dependency-kind-blocks declared 241 and observed 243, dependency-kind-related-to declared 43 and observed 50, both reporting ok true with reason retired_with_owner. The third retired declaration, graph-finding-legacy-ordering-cycle, observed 49 against a declared 49 and had not drifted.

Timeline reconstructed from dependency row created_at values. The rows that carried both populations past their ceilings were written on 2026-08-08 between 21:55Z and 22:50Z by ordinary maintenance sessions through the supported surface. Both owning items reached closed at roughly 23:25Z the same evening. The breach therefore existed for about ninety minutes while the bounds were still enforced, and was never reported, because the next evaluation ran after retirement.

Both fixes verified genuine, in a sandbox tracker at this commit, so that neither retirement is mistaken for a bad decision. Writing a dependency of kind related_to now stores kind related, confirming that pm-4020c5's canonical write contract shipped and that this population can no longer grow. A reverse blocks row now classifies its dependent as blocked under pm next, confirming that pm-jkbqt8's corpus-aware reverse resolution shipped and that blocks rows are no longer invisible to readiness. The decisions were right; the vocabulary had no state in which to record them, so the only available outcome was silence.

Contrast that motivated the fix. The surface replication gate in the same directory honours a waiver only while it names a pm item and carries an expires_on that is greater than or equal to today, so a suppression there decays and enforcement resumes. The measurement ratchet had the inverse lifetime: the bound decayed and enforcement ended permanently. Two gates, one directory, opposite polarities, nothing reconciling them.

Change shipped. Declarations now carry an on_owner_terminal disposition. The default is hold, so a bound keeps comparing after its owner closes or is canceled. Setting it to retire stops the comparison and requires a non-empty retired_reason, so dropping a guard is a recorded decision; a retirement without a reason fails with retirement_reason_missing. A disposition outside the domain fails with owner_terminal_disposition_not_declared rather than falling back to the default, because silently defaulting an unreadable disposition is how a guard disappears without anyone deciding it should. The re-baseline path still skips explicitly retired declarations and now re-baselines held ones like any other, tighten-only in both polarities. The failure text no longer advises moving the owning item to a terminal status, which was the exact escape hatch this item was filed about.

Both drifted bounds re-declared at their true current counts, 243 and 50, measured on 2026-08-09, each with a note recording that its fix shipped, that the sandbox probe confirmed it, and why the population is now held rather than retired. related_to is held rather than retired even though it can no longer grow, because holding a frozen population costs nothing and is precisely what would catch a regression in the write-time canonicalization.

Result. The gate now reports twenty-six enforced, three of them held past a finished owner, and zero retired, against twenty-three enforced and three retired before. Two populations that were unguarded are guarded again at their true values.

Negative control extended from two declarations to four, and passes. The two lifetime controls are the ones that could not have passed before: negative-control-held-past-closed-owner declares a ceiling of zero owned by a closed item and reports ceiling_exceeded, proving a terminal owner no longer stops the comparison, and negative-control-retirement-without-reason reports retirement_reason_missing. The held control is identified by declaration id rather than by reason, because it shares ceiling_exceeded with the plain ceiling control and the property it proves is that the comparison ran at all.

Incidental correction to a standing note. pm create does accept --close-reason. The negative control's seeded closed owner was refused with close_reason_required under governance.require_close_reason, and the refusal envelope named the flag in its own examples, which is a small piece of evidence that closed value domains that teach their own recovery are reachable today.

patch.value: Bound lifetime declared independently of owner lifecycle, defaulting to continued enforcement

Declared owner-terminal disposition shipped: bounds hold past a finished owner by default, explicit retirement requires a recorded reason, cancellation no longer silences a guard, and both drifted populations are re-declared and held at 243 and 50. Gate moved from 23 enforced with 3 retired to 26 enforced with 0 retired; negative control extended to four declarations and proves a held bound still fails after its owner closed.

A declaration keeps enforcing after its owning item reaches a terminal status unless it explicitly declares retirement with a recorded reason, and the two populations that drifted while unguarded are held at their true counts.

Shipped. on_owner_terminal defaults to hold; retire requires a non-empty retired_reason and fails as retirement_reason_missing without one; an out-of-domain disposition fails rather than defaulting. dependency-kind-blocks re-declared 241 to 243 and dependency-kind-related-to 43 to 50, both held. Gate reports 26 enforced, 3 held, 0 retired against 23 enforced and 3 retired before. Negative control extended to four declarations, including one proving a held bound still fails after its owner closed.

value.text: CI escape on the first push, fixed in the follow-up. Two jobs failed at commit f6deae17c. Gates (static) reported evaluateDeclaration at complexity 17 against a cap of 16, because the added disposition fields each carry optional chaining and optional chaining counts toward the cap; the invariant half of the observation is now built by resolveObservationBase, which is the same remedy the ratchet's earlier polarity work used when nested ternaries hit 24. Gates (coverage) reported 99.99 percent, from the one branch the new negative control cannot reach on a passing run: the failure path asserting that the held bound was proved against a closed owner specifically. A fiftieth test now drives it by seeding the terminal owner as canceled, so both lifetime reasons still fire while the closed-owner assertion does not, which is the only state that isolates that branch. Local verification afterwards: eslint clean, full lint clean, coverage exactly 100/100/100/100 with zero uncovered counts, tracker ratchet 26 enforced with 3 held and 0 retired, negative control passing all four declarations. Worth recording that pnpm quality:static passed locally throughout and never runs eslint, so the complexity cap is reachable only through pnpm lint or hosted CI - a local and hosted gap of the same shape as pm-xgah3a, and the reason the escape was not caught before pushing.
